clue.text: Meet as one is following good movie

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
Spielberg's film about the extra-terrestrial
acting as one means acting jointly

explanation.surface: Someone joins a group heading off to see a good film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' reads as a verb but is the noun, as in a hunt meet; the film is Spielberg's alien classic.
explanation.definitionFit: A meet, as in a hunt or sports meeting, is a gathering, which is what a get-together is.

clue.text: Leave the drink on purpose, revealing rage

definitions.note: verb sense: to fly into a fury

blocks.note: literal reading: deliberately jump into the swimming pool where the water is deepest
idiomatic reading: to lose your temper violently

explanation.surface: Someone storms off from the pub deliberately, making their anger plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for water, here a swimming pool; leaping in at the deep end is the literal sense of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes suddenly losing control and becoming furious, a colloquial synonym for raging.

clue.text: The ones with time to get stockings on?

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
hose is an old collective word for stockings

explanation.surface: A question about which people have time to pull their stockings on.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the time letter on top of the stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun 'those' points to particular people or things, as in 'those who wait'.

clue.text: Late but expected to have finished first

blocks.note: when something is finished it is over
a train that is expected is due

explanation.surface: Someone is late though they were expected to be done by now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' moves the word for finished ahead of the word for expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment or arrival past its scheduled time is overdue, i.e. late.

clue.text: Support tip on rambling rose

indicators.note: a rambling plant sprawls in no set order, so these letters wander out of place

blocks.note: the tip of something is its end
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on how to prop up a rambling rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling rose' is a real kind of climbing rose, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or product is to back it publicly, a direct synonym for support.

clue.text: Holy greeting before you get married

blocks.note: a variant spelling of hello
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: A sacred greeting exchanged just before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is consecrated, made sacred, so it means holy.

clue.text: Ball, rarely loath to dance, is a capital entertainer

indicators.note: set to dance, the letters move about the floor into new positions

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone seldom reluctant to dance at a ball is a first-rate entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like slang for excellent, but it means in the capital: the Royal Albert Hall is a famous London concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The concert hall in London entertains audiences, so it is cheekily called an entertainer located in the capital city.

clue.text: Spend no end on ceremony for brownie?

indicators.note: 'no' says the word that follows it is removed from spend

blocks.note: taken as written before cutting
the letters of the word end, which are taken away
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Advice not to spend endlessly on a Brownie's ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' does not mean drop the last letter: the actual letters E, N, D are removed from Spend. A brownie in folklore is a household elf.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a helpful household goblin of folklore, and a sprite is any elf or fairy.

clue.text: Journalist tried working outside job centre

indicators.note: working suggests being put into operation in a new arrangement
outside says one set of letters goes around the other
centre picks out only the middle letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the middle letter of job

explanation.surface: A reporter tried working at a job centre, where unemployed people look for work.
explanation.walkthrough: A job centre is a British government office for jobseekers; the phrase splits so 'centre' acts on job alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and selects material for publication.

clue.text: Incense is all right during show

indicators.note: something happening during a show sits within it

blocks.note: to show something is to prove it
OK is short for all right

explanation.surface: A remark that burning incense during a performance is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' reads as the fragrant noun but is the verb, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them angry, just as to provoke them is to goad them.

clue.text: Ballad in act is put off until later

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: a deed is an act
a lay is a narrative poem or ballad

explanation.surface: A ballad in a stage act gets postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something postponed to a later time has been delayed, a straightforward synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Fired Neil for upsetting cricketer

indicators.note: upsetting overturns the letters into a different order

blocks.note: both words used as fodder

explanation.surface: Neil was sacked for annoying a cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: An infielder is a fielding player stationed close to the batsman, so a type of cricketer.

clue.text: Little bird now lets things slip a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a fragment of the run of words is taken

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A small bird has started letting things slide a little.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so literally a little bird.

clue.text: A sound return from city head office

blocks.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London
HO is the standard abbreviation for head office

explanation.surface: A solid reply comes back from headquarters in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'reliable', but it is the noise that comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a reflected noise, a sound that returns to the listener.

clue.text: Made rebel clear off, being a bit brainy?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'being a bit brainy' means relating to a part of the brain

indicators.note: off implies the letters have gone wrong and fallen out of order

blocks.note: both words used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone clever got a rebel to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit brainy' is a pun: not slightly clever, but belonging to a bit of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebellar describes the cerebellum, one part of the brain, so it concerns a piece of the brain.

clue.text: Jolson supporter takes poor actor into Spanish palace

indicators.note: takes ... into means one piece is placed within the others

blocks.note: Al Jolson, the American singer
a ham is a bad, overacting performer
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A fan of Al Jolson brings a bad actor into a Spanish palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'into' after poor actor marks where it goes: between the singer's name and the supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Personal cover for those in retirement?

definitions.text: Personal cover for those in retirement?

blocks.clueFragment: Personal cover for those in retirement
blocks.note: surface reading: insurance or a pension plan for retired people
setter's reading: people who have retired for the night, i.e. gone to bed, and what covers them there

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' and 'retirement' suggest insurance and pensions; 'retire' also means go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets, blankets and duvets are the linen that covers a sleeper lying in bed.

clue.text: Spot famous model and ring drunk

blocks.note: a blot is a spot of ink
the Model T was Ford's famous car
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Seeing a celebrated model and phoning her while intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous model is a car, not a fashion model: Ford's Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely intoxicated.

clue.text: Thanks volunteers taking fellow to iron material

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks
F is the abbreviation for fellow
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers are thanked for getting a man to do the ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: The volunteers take the fellow and iron in front of them, so their letters come last.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric, often silk, so a kind of material.

clue.text: It stretches lace and it's in need of adjustment

indicators.note: needing adjustment means the letters must be moved into a better order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A piece of stretchy lace has to be readjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic is stretchy cord or material, the thing that stretches and springs back.

clue.text: Aviators reversed bearing in alarm

indicators.note: reversed tells us to write the airmen's abbreviation backwards
in places the compass point inside the other letters

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force
east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Pilots turned back, steering a course in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and alarm are both sudden feelings of fright or apprehension, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Live there, having abandoned the party

definitions.note: a jokey reading: RE-SIDE, to choose a side afresh

blocks.note: first meaning: to dwell in a place
second meaning, split as two parts: someone who has quit their party must take a side again

explanation.surface: Someone stays on in a place after walking out of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half only works by splitting the word into RE- and SIDE: a defector re-sides with another party.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to make one's home there, i.e. to live in that place.

clue.text: Ring through with article on musical entertainment

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped
per means by way of, through
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A phone call about an article on a show with music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' is also Wagner's operatic cycle, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged drama set to music, a form of musical entertainment.

clue.text: People sharing accommodation, even couples

definitions.note: a punning reading split into two words

blocks.note: first meaning: people who share a rented flat
second meaning read as two words: flat (level, even) and mates (pairs, couples)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is the British word for an apartment, and also means even; 'mates' are pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatmates are housemates who rent an apartment together, sharing its accommodation.

clue.text: Staff try to get fruit

blocks.note: to staff a desk is to man it
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Employees attempt to pick some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun for employees but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a sweet tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Doctor left timber supplier outside to shiver

indicators.note: outside means one item wraps around the others

blocks.note: trees supply timber
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A doctor left a timber merchant out in the cold to shiver.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to shake involuntarily, much as one does when shivering from cold or fear.

clue.text: Part-time soldiers drank liquid ? from this?

definitions.text: Part-time soldiers drank liquid ? from this?

indicators.note: liquid flows freely, so these letters run into a new shape

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's part-time reserve
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Reservists knocking back beer, and asking what vessel they drank from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: what soldiers drank liquid from. The stray question mark in the middle is as the source prints it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, typically for beer, the vessel soldiers would drink from.

clue.text: Where one is taught to play well?

definitions.text: Where one is taught to play well?

blocks.clueFragment: Where one is taught to play well
blocks.note: surface reading: a music lesson or sports coaching
setter's reading: to play a role on stage, so where actors train

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests sport or an instrument; it is acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors train at institutions teaching stagecraft, where students learn to perform roles convincingly.
